classification.difficultyReason: Model a three-sided fencing constraint, form an area inequality and interpret its single feasible solution as dimensions.

content.prompt: A farmer needs to build a rectangular holding pen for some sheep. The side of a barn will be used for one side of the pen and there is $56\text{ m}$ of fencing available for the remaining three sides. Let $x$ be the length of each side perpendicular to the barn wall.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find an expression for the third side in terms of $x$ and draw a diagram showing all this information.

answer.worked: The two perpendicular sides use $2x$ metres of fencing, leaving $(56-2x)\text{ m}$ for the third side.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13a; answer diagram on teacher PDF page 25
spec.description: Rectangular pen with the barn wall along its upper side, two perpendicular fenced sides labelled x and the opposite fenced side labelled 56−2x. Decorative brickwork omitted.
spec.mathematics: The three fenced sides total x+x+(56−2x)=56 metres.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student must construct the diagram.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The area $A$ of the pen must be at least $392\text{ m}^2$ so that the sheep are not overcrowded. What are the possible dimensions of the pen?

answer.short:
$14\text{ m}\times28\text{ m}$, with the $28\text{ m}$ side parallel to the barn wall.

The area inequality is satisfied only when $x=14$.
answer.worked:
For a non-degenerate pen, $0<x<28$. Its area is $A=x(56-2x)$ square metres.
$$\begin{align*}x(56-2x)&\ge392\\-2x^2+56x-392&\ge0\\x^2-28x+196&\le0\\(x-14)^2&\le0\end{align*}$$
A square is non-negative, so the inequality holds only at its zero, $x=14$. The third side is $56-2(14)=28\text{ m}$. Thus the only possible dimensions are $14\text{ m}\times28\text{ m}$.
